key_insight: Multiwavelength photoluminescence reveals that PEABF4 treatment initially reduces interfacial recombination but accelerates degradation under thermal aging, with losses spreading into the perovskite absorber.
engineering_relevance: Nondestructive, depth-sensitive recombination measurements can help engineers evaluate passivation strategies for both initial performance and thermal stability.
method: Compare photoluminescence decay under multiple excitation wavelengths.
Track interface- and bulk-dominated recombination during thermal aging.
Interpret decay signatures using diffusion–recombination simulations.
evidence_signal: PL measurements indicate reduced recombination from fullerene deposition after PEABF4 treatment, but faster degradation during thermal aging; simulations support distinguishing changes in surface recombination velocity and bulk lifetime.
watch_item: Depth assignments rely on model-supported interpretation of PL signals, and the abstract provides no quantitative degradation rates or device-lifetime validation.
paper_title: Wavelength-Dependent Photoluminescence Mapping of Depth-Dependent Degradation Under Thermal Stress in Phenethylammonium Tetrafluoroborate Treated Perovskite Solar Cells
